title: Script: Disk Usage Alert in Bash

scenes.line1: Ever caught a full disk too late?
scenes.line2: How do you script a warning?
scenes.say: Ever found out your disk was full only after things broke? How would you script a warning before that happens?

scenes.label: Skills
scenes.sub: Parsing, loops, thresholds, exit codes—one script.
scenes.say: This task shows off your ability to parse output, loop through results, set thresholds, and handle exit codes, all in one script.

scenes.title: Check disk usage with Bash
scenes.say: Here's a script that checks every filesystem. If any go over eighty five percent, it prints a warning and sets the exit code to one.

rows.b: So cron or monitoring can alert

scenes.say: First, it runs the disk free command. Then, it skips temporary filesystems. For each one, it checks if usage is above your threshold. If so, it warns and exits non-zero so jobs or monitoring can catch it.

scenes.question: Why return a non-zero exit code?
scenes.right: So monitoring tools or cron jobs can detect a problem and alert you
scenes.say: Here's a common interview trap: Why does the script return a non-zero exit code? It's so monitoring tools or cron jobs know there's a problem and can alert you.
